Definition: from G3844 and G190; to follow near, i.e. (figuratively) attend (as a result), trace out, conform to:--attain, follow, fully know, have understanding.
BiblicalUsage: Parakoloutheō means to follow closely, to trace carefully, to attend to. Luke writes his gospel having had perfect understanding of all things from the very first, and Paul tells Timothy, Thou hast fully known my doctrine, manner of life, purpose, faith, longsuffering, charity, patience.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that following closely is how truth is handed on: Luke traces everything from the first, and Timothy watches Paul's whole life, not just his sermons.
